title: Split data for later checks
summary: train_test_split divides a dataset into training and test parts. A seed makes this split repeatable for the same data and tool behaviour.
introduction: train_test_split divides a dataset into training and test parts. A seed makes this split repeatable for the same data and tool behaviour. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain split data for later checks
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: train_test_split divides a dataset into training and test parts. A seed makes this split repeatable for the same data and tool behaviour.

blocks.code:
from datasets import Dataset
data = Dataset.from_dict({"text": ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]})
parts = data.train_test_split(test_size=2, seed=7)
print(parts["train"].num_rows, parts["test"].num_rows)
blocks.title: Split data for later checks

blocks.text: The output is 4 2. test_size=2 requests two rows, leaving four for training. This tiny split is only a procedure demonstration.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A repeatable split is not automatically a fair split for every task.
